about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Ashley Moody

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CHARLOTTE WOODWARD ORGAN TRANSPLANT DISCRIMINATION PREVENTION ACT
statements.title: CHARLOTTE WOODWARD ORGAN TRANSPLANT DISCRIMINATION PREVENTION ACT
sentences: Mr. President, notwithstanding rule XXII, I ask unanimous consent that the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee be discharged from further consideration of H.R. 1520 and the Senate proceed to its immediate consideration.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: And I believe the frustration--maybe even the lack of trust--in Congress stems from the fact that they believe that we have not rolled up our sleeves every single day and been mindful that that is our first duty.
Let's deliver a no stock trading ban.

I came here today and said: Let's honor our veterans tomorrow, those that served us that said, ``I will put my life on the line for you, this country, the fundamental idea that a free people can govern ourselves and live together with safety and security and our rights protected.'' They stood up for that.

I am going to introduce a resolution to honor our veterans and recognize Veterans Day, and I believe that we can do more than just file a resolution and announce that we are going to all, as a country, respect Veterans Day.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Constitution Day (Executive Session)
statements.title: Constitution Day (Executive Session)
sentences: You don't like a decision from the Supreme Court?
Pack the Court, add Justices until you get the decisions you want.
Pressure private companies to silence them and call it fighting misinformation.
They want to abolish the Supreme Court, replace the Presidency, abolish the electoral college.
Again and again, we will see the same pattern when constitutional guardrails stand between you and what you want: Simply move the guardrails.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: The SAVE America Act--indeed, election integrity efforts--are grounded in a simple, commonsense--indeed, foundational--principle that only American citizens should vote in American elections.
Americans must be able to trust that their elections are not corrupted or skewed or nullified by noncitizens voting or ineligible persons voting.
Questions about election integrity are not new.
It is the responsibility of Congress to uphold the election integrity of this country.
Look at any of the election integrity measures that are coming up.
I am proud to have been an original sponsor of the SAVE America Act, but voter ID and voter integrity bills--all of these are important.
How do we ensure only citizens vote?
The answer is so simple: voter ID.
According to the Pew Research Center, 83 percent of Americans support voter ID laws--83 percent.
The very groups that Democrats claim would be harmed by this measure support voter ID.
It is also important to remember we have just seen the headlines out of New Jersey where thousands of noncitizens were registered to vote through the State's motor vehicle system.
It is further proof as to why the SAVE America Act is needed.
You had better be darned sure I am going to do that here as a U.S. Senator on behalf of all Americans.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Working Families Tax Cut Act (Executive Session)
statements.title: Working Families Tax Cut Act (Executive Session)
sentences: We just celebrated not only the birthday of this Nation--250 years--but we also celebrated the anniversary of the Working Families Tax Cut Act being signed into law.
We got together with law enforcement officers--hundreds of them-- where we highlighted no tax on overtime.

For the nurse or, as we discussed, for the law enforcement officer picking up extra shifts, the linemen that so often have to come in and restore power in Florida after storms--when they are putting in extra hours--factory workers putting in extra hours to support their families, that no tax on overtime rewards hard work instead of taxing it.
And so I argued very hard for the provisions that eliminated taxes on Social Security benefits and provided additional relief through the enhanced deductions for seniors.
So I just want to underscore what that meant--that Working Families Tax Cut Act--just this past filing season.
But if you don't touch that original investment, by the time they are 18 and they are on their own, you can use it for a vacation, for a downpayment on a house.

So when you are hearing about all of the fraud that we keep uncovering or where we sent millions of dollars to some foreign country to help some crazy program for foreign nationals, today, Americans can go to irs.gov/trumpaccounts and sign up and get $1,000 for their kids.
So in addition to these accounts, 40 million families have taken advantage of the enhanced child tax credit that we permanently doubled and expanded through the Working Families Tax Cut Act.

And through this Working Families Tax Cut Act, of which we are now celebrating the 1-year anniversary--and many of the provisions that we all fought hard for, over on this side of the aisle, are now just going into effect--we also made sure that there was a Federal tax credit scholarship that could help millions of students across the Nation get education of their parents' choice.
We started with our first school-choice statute.

But even for States where you have universal school choice--and there are a few of us like Florida, but others have started with school-choice statutes--understanding that each child learns differently, you can still take advantage of the Working Families Tax Cut Act because it allows for the deduction of education expenses for tutoring, for technology, and for so many of those supplemental education expenses that come along with education that parents choose.
So Floridians are still winning, even though we already have school choice.
As my State's newest Senator, this was an important piece of legislation for many reasons, and I will share what it has meant for hard-working Floridians.
And we are uncovering, day in and day out--and we will continue to do so--exposing where some of those choices went awry and where some of those choices led to corruption and crime.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SENATE RESOLUTION 773--RECOGNIZING FATHER'S DAY AND THE ROLE A FATHER PLAYS IN THE LIVES OF CHILDREN AND ADULTS
statements.title: SENATE RESOLUTION 773--RECOGNIZING FATHER'S DAY AND THE ROLE A FATHER PLAYS IN THE LIVES OF CHILDREN AND ADULTS
sentences: In fact, when I became the attorney general of the great free State of Florida, I had a young child at home, and my husband, who is a true hero, a hero dad--he is a career law enforcement officer--really stepped up.
My husband Justin works long hours as a law enforcement officer, as you can see.

I remember so many times when my law enforcement husband would go away for extended periods of time--whether it was to become a firearms instructor with the DEA or when he went to the National Academy at Quantico for months--he would come home--fly late at night--to make sports games or to help with homework.
I have introduced that for the Record, and it is an honor to do so.
I have also benefited from having father figures in my extended family that have played a large role in my success in life, and I will always be grateful.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Everything that they are espousing is subversive to the strength and security of this Nation, whether that is abolish ICE, whether that is defund the police, whether that is destroy our borders and roll out a welcome mat.

And that is why I have introduced a resolution to forbid taxpayers dollars for reimbursement of Member travel home during a lapse in government funding because if we are asking Federal employees to deal with uncertainty, if we are asking our ICE officers and Border Patrol to continue doing their jobs without clarity, if we are asking TSA agents to continue showing up without clarity, we should be willing to stay here and do ours.

They want to go back to how things were under the previous administration, you know, when they broke down all security measures at the border, when they made it open borders, when they demoralized and undermined law enforcement.
We now have thousands of people that were on the Terrorist Watchlist that were ushered in by the Biden administration, and we know that they released them and pushed them into this country.

So in the middle of an armed conflict, we have people in this country right now that were on the Terrorist Watchlist that were released by the last administration, and the Democrats' response is to not fund the folks that were going to go out and find them.

Let's talk about the 22-year-old Laken Riley, who was killed by an illegal immigrant in Georgia, or the 18-year-old college freshman Sheridan Gorman, shot and killed in a random attack by an illegal immigrant in Chicago.
And yet we will debate again whether we are going to give them the resources they need to do their jobs.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Department of Homeland Security (Executive Session)
statements.title: Department of Homeland Security (Executive Session)
sentences: Due to my Democratic defund disorder colleagues, the political antics they have thrown up to block funding for this incredibly important Agency is being done at the expense of protecting Americans.
Floridians and Americans alike know that my colleagues on the other side of the aisle are pushing a shutdown of DHS funding because they don't want a secure border.
This is about blasting apart the security structure President Trump has rebuilt after Biden destroyed the border.

For 4 long years, we watched as the previous administration disregarded the law and sowed chaos and destruction at our southern border, allowing a historic surge-- historic; some say up to 20 million people, many unvetted--to pour into this country.
The shutdown has been dragging on so long because my colleagues on the Democratic side of the aisle cannot stand that the border is now secure again and DHS is doing its job.
They cannot stand that the border isn't wide open.
They can't stand that unmitigated illegal immigration has been halted.
Because of this, they are throwing a temper tantrum, disguising this shutdown as anything other than what it is, and that is a mission to defund police.
Narcoterrorist cartels were enabled to bring massive amounts of deadly substances like fentanyl into our neighborhoods.
That once wide-open border was closed by Trump.
On day one, he took unprecedented action to close the border and started enforcing the law again.
He took action against the drug cartels and the flow of fentanyl and other dangerous drugs to keep our communities safe.
Under President Trump, DHS provided the most secure border in American history.
It is such a stark difference in what the border looked like under the Biden years to what it looks like today.
In fact, during the last month of the Biden administration, every single month saw more than 100,000 illegal immigrant encounters at the southwest border.
And we know that approximately 85 percent of those immigrants apprehended at the border were released into our interior.

The judge who sided with Florida's lawsuit when I took Biden to court and stood up against the illegal actions of his radical administration--that judge who sided with Florida said it best: Biden ``turned the Southwest Border into . . . little more than a speed bump.'' ``[L]ittle more than a speed bump.'' Then the American people fought back and elected President Donald Trump.
Total border apprehensions under the Trump administration's first year in office were lower than a single average month under the Biden administration.

In addition to the millions of unvetted illegal immigrants Biden let into our country, according to at least 1 recent report that, shockingly, the mainstream media isn't reporting, they allowed 18,000 known or suspected terrorists into the United States.
The current DHS shutdown is affecting President Trump's effort to get the unprecedented number of undocumented immigrants that may be a threat to this Nation and to our people out.
We know that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has been instrumental in preventing terror threats, removing more than 1,500 known or suspected terrorists.

One of the saddest things that I think we learned after the last administration, and certainly as a mother--not just as Florida's attorney general but as a mother--we watched as hundreds of thousands of unaccompanied minors were trafficked across the border by cartels, and then the Biden administration took the last step--shipped them all over the country.
Too many of these children were exploited and abused before, during, and after they came across that border with cartel members.
They wanted to secure our border, and now my Democratic colleagues are obstructing the will of the American people by saying: Oh yeah?

We are going to defund the police, we are going to defund those agents at the border, and we are going to defund those within that are protecting your communities and helping get those that are here right now--we saw this in Chicago last week; a murder by someone here, let in by the Biden administration-- here illegally--of a young college student again.
And they want to tie the hands of the law enforcement officials charged with getting them out.
That is nothing more than defunding the police that have taken oaths to protect you and your family.

People are going without paychecks, people that are doing very important jobs, like our TSA officers, like our law enforcement officers, like our personnel at the border, thousands that are charged with keeping this country safe.
I will always show up on this floor and make sure that the American people know who we are fighting for.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAFEGUARD AMERICAN VOTER ELIGIBILITY ACT--Continued
statements.title: SAFEGUARD AMERICAN VOTER ELIGIBILITY ACT--Continued
sentences: Mr. President, I know how hard the Presiding Officer and so many of our colleagues have worked to get the SAVE America Act to the floor.
That is why the issue before us--the SAVE America Act--is so important.
So Americans must trust that their elections are not corrupted or skewed or nullified by noncitizens or fraudulent voting.
Eighty-three percent of Americans support voter ID laws.
In fact, the people they profess to be protecting in some way have come out and said they want voter ID--the very people they think this will harm.
Questions about election integrity are not new.
They will fly off to other nation-states to defend noncitizens.
For the life of me, I think they are even putting their necks out there for cartels time and time again.
In fact, the States that have implemented voter ID laws did not see participation decline.

The SAVE America Act helps to reinforce trust in our elections, but it is about more than this one bill; it is about preserving the great experiment of the United States of America, of ``we the people'' governing ourselves and doing so through our duly elected officers.
Because of that, regardless of what party you identify as supporting, I urge my colleagues to pass the SAVE America Act.
But when it comes to American citizens and having their backs: We are going to fight it.
We are fighting it for somebody.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed
statements.title: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed
sentences: I am so proud to honor him today with a ``Florida's Finest Award.'' This is not somebody who dedicated his professional career in law enforcement.
This award honors Floridians and law enforcement officers who demonstrate selfless courage and go above and beyond to save lives.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAVE America Act (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: SAVE America Act (Executive Calendar)
sentences: I rise today to, in fact, speak on behalf of American citizens and in support of the rule of law, and I rise to say that we have to pass without delay the SAVE America Act.
Retaining election integrity should not be a partisan issue; it is foundational to our self-government.
The SAVE America Act upholds the rule of law.
We must preserve our elections to preserve our Republic, and that is why it is so important that we pass the SAVE America Act.
Mr. President, I rise today in support of what should be a given.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed--Resumed
statements.title: DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed--Resumed
sentences: The world owes a debt to Mr. Brewton and to his generation that can never be repaid.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRACK Act (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: TRACK Act (Executive Calendar)
sentences: So to streamline it and make it more clear, I introduced legislation called the TRACK Act.
I introduced this along with Senator Alsobrooks.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Mr. President, as you may know, we are recognizing National School Choice Week, and I thank my colleague for organizing those of us who believe dearly in educational options for children to come to the floor and speak about what we have accomplished and what we hope to accomplish on behalf of America's kids.

We went from having graduation rates at just 60 percent, with less than 1 percent of K through 12 students attending a public charter school, and fewer than 10 students in the State receiving a K through 12 scholarship in 1999.
We were one of the first States, a few years ago, to adopt universal school choice.

Close to 1 in 8 of our students now attends a public charter school--a public charter school--and more than 450,000 students receive some form of K through 12 scholarship, including the Florida Tax Credit Scholarship.
For our children in Florida, school choice has been an invaluable tool for success no matter their background, their means, or what ZIP Code they live in.
I have been a proud champion of the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which is now, I am proud to say, signed into law.

Not only do Florida kids have access to all of the options that we have provided to them through State law, but they now have access to supplemental resources that were provided through the Education Freedom Tax Credit.

As we wrap up National School Choice Week, we must remember and keep advocating publicly because there are some States that have the opportunity to opt in but refuse to do so, and that breaks my heart for the many kids who could benefit from what is available to them through educational choice.
That is why I commit to continuing to advocate for school choice--so that all of America's kids see the same opportunities that we have been able to offer to the children of Florida.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: No matter where you are politically--Republican or Democrat, pro-life or pro-choice--one thing I think we can all agree on is that the more information for women making life-changing decisions, the better.
For these reasons, I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to vote in favor of my Pregnant Students' Rights Act to support young mothers and protect life.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: As you know, last week we celebrated Law Enforcement Appreciation Day, and I wanted to recognize two great officers from the Tampa Bay area, where I, as one of the newest U.S. Senators, hail from.
Last month, Tampa Police Department Officers Jason Sikoski and Kaleb Girard saved an 86-year-old man who was found dangling off of his roof.
And so you can imagine the quick response from Tampa Police Officers Sikoski and Girard, along with fire rescue, who showed up.

Certainly, as attorney general of Florida before I came to the Senate a year ago, I had always recognized law enforcement for their courage, for dedicating their professional lives to enforcing the people's law.
Our Florida's Finest Award honors those Floridians and law enforcement officers who demonstrate selfless courage, who go above and beyond to save lives.
I am so thankful that these Tampa police officers saved this man's life and for all they do every day to keep the Tampa community safe.
I will end by saying that each and every one of our law enforcement officers is essential to upholding the rule of law, the people's law.

I will keep standing up for the men and women of law enforcement, every law enforcement officer, because we know that they are essential not only for a stronger and safer Florida but for a stronger and safer United States of America.
Pursuant to rule XXII, the Chair lays before the Senate the pending cloture motion, which the clerk will state.

The legislative clerk read as follows: Cloture Motion We, the undersigned Senators, in accordance with the provisions of rule XXII of the Standing Rules of the Senate, do hereby move to bring to a close debate on Calendar No. 299, H.R. 6938, a bill making consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Minnesota ICE Shooting (Executive Session)
statements.title: Minnesota ICE Shooting (Executive Session)
sentences: Mr. President, tomorrow is Law Enforcement Appreciation Day, and it was my intention to come to the floor today and talk about some great officers and celebrate the men and women that put their lives on the line to protect us every day.
I can tell you that firsthand as the wife of a law enforcement officer.
It is a very dangerous situation in some of these missions and law enforcement activities.

That is why I introduced the Halo Act back in November because, as I saw the threats of political violence, of threats against our law enforcement officers were rapidly increasing, I knew that we had to do something.

It is deeply troubling to hear the anti-law enforcement rhetoric being used by so many when it comes to Federal officers simply trying to show up and do the jobs that we, as a nation, hired them to do.

It is part of this broader pattern of coordinated efforts, encouraged by elected politicians who keep increasing their rhetoric and almost encouraging--let me just take the ``almost'' out, encouraging people to get in the way of law enforcement officers trying to do their job, knowing how dangerous that is, not only dangerous for law enforcement officers but for those who show up and try to impede their efforts.
According to the Department of Homeland Security, assaults on police are up 1,300 percent, death threats on police up 8,000 percent.
And we must send a message that targeted attacks, interference with the duties of officers, threat, harm, violence against law enforcement must end.
Ahead of Law Enforcement Appreciation Day, we have to acknowledge that without the men and women that put on that badge every day, this would not be the country that we know.
And so I introduced the Halo Act so that one of these events wouldn't occur.
That is what is attracting people from around the United States of America to my home State, the great free State of Florida, because we support them.
In fact, we introduced legislation and passed legislation to give them a safety zone, a buffer zone to do their jobs and do them safely.
The Halo Act, which I introduced 2 months ago, will ensure that Federal officers can perform their duties without fear of intimidation, interference, or violence.
I urge my colleagues to join me and support the Halo Act to have our officers' back, to ensure our communities are safe and that they can do their jobs.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HALO ACT
statements.title: HALO ACT
sentences: Two young National Guardsmen, who had served their country like the Presiding Officer, who were doing their jobs of keeping us safe, were ambushed by a gunman here on asylum.

Last week--just a few days ago--in my home State of Florida, Sergeant Erik LeVasseur, from Port St. Lucie, while doing his job as a law enforcement officer, was shot in the face when he responded to a call for help.

Unfortunately, a tragedy like this is happening time and time again in a growing stream of incidents across our country, wherein our Nation's guardians, with whatever badge they wear and whatever oath they have taken--from our guardsmen to our Federal law enforcement, to our State law enforcement heroes--are being targeted.
From January 21, 2024, through November 21, 2024, there were only 19 recorded assaults against ICE law enforcement.
At the same time this year, ICE law enforcement has faced 238 reported assaults.
It is a 1,153-percent increase in assaults on those law enforcement officers.

Incredibly, incredibly radical, Democrat-led cities and States in this country are using taxpayer money to encourage the harassment and obstruction of our law enforcement officers in the United States of America.
You know, personally, I am the wife of a law enforcement officer.
This act is modeled after something we have done in my great home State of Florida, where we are the most pro-law enforcement State in the Nation.

That is why not only are we leading in the Nation in people wanting to move to our State for protection, the people who are doing that protection, our law enforcement officers, are coming from all over this Nation, uprooting their families, to be Florida heroes because they know we have their back.

It takes a truly special person to answer that call, whether that is in our military or in our law enforcement professions--and I am proud to be the wife of a law enforcement officer--to be the one that runs towards danger to help others like that courageous National Guard major last week.

I just introduced the Halo Act to protect Federal officers while they conduct their official duties, and I am proud to say that this week, more of my colleagues have signed up to cosponsor this important legislation.

For our heroes' sake, for our country's sake, for the success of this great American experiment, living as a free man under the rule of law, I urge my colleagues to have our officers' backs while they cover ours.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Trump appointees win again. Eight of the ten least partisan judges were nominated by President Trump.
statements.title: Trump appointees win again. Eight of the ten least partisan judges were nominated by President Trump.
sentences: On a Sunday morning in October, Officer Andrew Hinds was on regular patrol duty with the Riviera Police Department--Riviera Beach Police Department, they would correct me-- when he spotted smoke coming from a neighborhood.

Ever since I was Florida's attorney general, and now as our State's newest U.S. Senator, it has been important to me to continue to honor the extraordinary work of our selfless law enforcement officers that protect Floridians every day.
Our ``Florida's Finest'' award honors those Floridians and law enforcement officers who demonstrate selfless courage and go above and beyond in service to their fellow man.
I am so grateful for Officer Hinds and all of Florida's amazing law enforcement officers who, on a daily basis, put service above self.
Thank you for allowing me this moment, Mr. President, to recognize this incredible law enforcement officer with our ``Florida's Finest'' award.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: And that means our troops, Federal law enforcement officers, air traffic controllers, other essential personnel, families in need that go paycheck to paycheck aren't getting a paycheck.

We have Federal law enforcement officers working tirelessly to get deadly drugs out of our communities and take down dangerous gangs like Tren de Aragua, doing it for free without being paid, because my colleagues are using the American people as political leverage.

Our troops, our law enforcement officers, so many essential government employees are still working because the-- without pay--because the Democrats will not vote to open this government, and my Democratic colleagues are still getting their paychecks.
Maybe I should put this in terms that even my Democratic colleagues can understand: Maybe the Senate needs to reimagine the filibuster.
So I urge my colleagues to end this shutdown.

That is why I am cosponsoring the Eliminate Shutdowns Act and other legislation that would make sure this does not happen again and ensures that our government remains open and those heroes that put their lives on the line for us get paid.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Mr. President, I rise to the podium today to address my colleagues as we are headed into one of the darkest times of the year, when daylight saving time ends and our clocks fall back 1 hour.
Most countries don't even observe daylight saving time.

In 2018, the great State of Florida, which leads the way on so many issues--the State where I am proud to say I am the newest U.S. Senator--Florida became the first State to call for year-round daylight saving time, but we need Congress to affirm this change through legislation.

In my experience as a parent dealing with a kid that wanted to be outside playing sports, who anxiously awaited his law enforcement father to come home and throw the baseball, not having that extra hour of daylight was really difficult, especially when all kids want to do, at the end of their day of school and chores, is to be outside.
Making daylight saving time permanent makes time together as a family outside with activities possible.
We can lock the clock, once and for all, by passing the Sunshine Protection Act that I have cosponsored with my fellow Florida Senator Rick Scott.
The Sunshine Protection Act has previously passed in the Senate unanimously.
This weekend, we will perform the outdated and unnecessary ritual of changing our clocks.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: The opposing Democrats do so while knowing they are voting against paying our troops for our security, against paying law enforcement for safety, and against paying so many other people that are necessary for critical functions.

Now, these tactics have evolved into obstructing government itself, to hold the pay of Federal law enforcement and our military hostage-- let alone the thousands of other Federal employees who continue to show up and fulfill their duties without pay.

In my home state of Florida, we are seeing crisis centers which serve veterans, law enforcement officers, first responders, some of our most vulnerable that encounter hardships, all because colleagues have refused to open the government.

And, finally, I want to take a moment to thank every single Federal employee continuing to work without pay: our servicemembers, Federal law enforcement officers, Coast Guard members, air traffic controllers, so many others--including our own staff, including the staff on the Senate floor that show up and stay up all night as the Democrats recite poetry.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Nomination of Jeanine Pirro (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: Nomination of Jeanine Pirro (Executive Calendar)
sentences: If we continue down this path, if we continue to allow obstruction at every turn or continue to allow people on the other side of the aisle to gain personal points or even political points, we weaken this body created by the Framers to carry out the responsibilities the American people have asked of us, protecting our liberty and protecting this Union.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: National Police Week (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: National Police Week (Executive Calendar)
sentences: I rise today in celebration of officers but with solemn reflection during National Police Week.
It is a time when our Nation pauses to honor the men and women of law enforcement and to remember those who have made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.
We are grateful that he is here, along with other men and women of law enforcement from Florida.
Police Week is more than a yearly tradition.

In Florida, I say time and time again--and we pride ourselves--we may have a bit of a debate and a friendly competition here, but I believe we will win--that we are the most pro-law enforcement State in the Nation.
Our leaders back the blue, tan, and green, and we do whatever it takes to help those brave officers do their jobs.
In honor of National Police Week, I was proud to join a bipartisan resolution designating May 11 through 17 as National Police Week.
This Police Week resolution reiterates our unwavering support for law enforcement officers across this Nation.

As Florida's former attorney general and the wife of a law enforcement officer, I have had the opportunity to work closely with so many brave men and women in law enforcement across Florida and indeed our Nation.

As the wife of a career law enforcement officer, I cannot imagine this loss or express words to ease the pain, but we offer our deepest gratitude and our support, and we are here for you in every way possible and thank you that you stood by them while they stood for us in ensuring our communities could live in peace and safety.

To every active-duty officer here in Washington, DC, here this week for National Police Week and those back at home protecting our communities right now as I am speaking on the Senate floor, thank you for your courage.

It is a promise that we will never forget, that we will never take for granted the courage it takes to wear that badge, and that we will never stop saying the names or praying for the families of those whom we have lost.
To the families, friends, and fellow officers of those we lost, we see you, we stand with you, we grieve with you, and we continue to pray for you.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TERMINATING THE NATIONAL EMERGENCY DECLARED TO IMPOSE GLOBAL TARIFFS
statements.title: TERMINATING THE NATIONAL EMERGENCY DECLARED TO IMPOSE GLOBAL TARIFFS
sentences: Their reckless regulatory agenda prioritized Green New Deal virtue signaling over good fiscal stewardship and the interests of the American people by exposing manufacturers and other stakeholders in our industries to regulatory uncertainty and forcing American families to shoulder the burden.
I would like to thank Congressman Craig Goldman of Texas for leading this effort in the House, and I urge my colleagues in the Senate to vote for this resolution.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Fentanyl (Executive Session)
statements.title: Fentanyl (Executive Session)
sentences: That is why we have to continue to provide law enforcement the tools they need to get this drug off our streets and make sure we are providing lifesaving medications like Naloxone to first responders and that people who are struggling with addiction know where to get help.
After 4 years of a wide-open border and free range given to drug cartels to smuggle illicit substances into our country, it is no surprise that our Nation was flooded with fentanyl.
Our law enforcement officers were up for the task.
I, back in 2023, called for the cartels to be labeled ``foreign terrorist organizations.'' President Biden ignored our call.
I called for the border to be closed and the then-head of DHS to be fired for allowing drug smugglers and countless amounts of fentanyl to flood our country.
